mechanism: #26 = #5 mirrored (L<->R), states renamed A..F -> D,E,A,B,C,F, but started in #5's state C.

template.note: Bouncer_v3 TM1 needs an eventually periodic side: RC i pumps exponents 363+128i and 1+3i, and one BigStep = 128 bounces checked by native computation. #26's edge is aperiodic with positive entropy, so no RC i exists. InfiniteRect_v1 (periodic boundary tokens) and LongNv1 (explicit exponent patterns) assume the same kind of regularity.

strategy: Park with #5 as one cryptid candidate: any erosion bound for #5 transfers verbatim through the mirror map, giving both kills. Cryptid protocol still owes a Rocq rule reduction (bounce + 7 rules + no-00 invariant); one file can do both twins.
risks: No deterministic erosion bound is known for the shared edge (#5 research: potentials miss by 5-12x).
#26's block is one cell shorter than #5's, so its halting threshold is one cell closer; irrelevant after bounce 40 (block >= 33).
The twin map is checked to 1e10 steps; its all-time proof is the mirror identity of the tables plus the wall-model argument.
